items.who: Holders of ETA-eligible passports, including Singapore and Malaysia, visiting for tourism or business visitor activities must get an ETA before travel.
items.fee: AUD 20 service charge in the Australian ETA app. No visa charge.
items.validity: 12 months or until the passport expires, whichever is first. Multiple entries, up to 3 months per visit.
steps: Download the official Australian ETA app from the Apple App Store or Google Play.
Scan your passport chip and take a live face photo in the app.
Answer the questions and pay the AUD 20 service charge.
Wait for the grant email before booking non-refundable travel.
items.note: Apply only through the official app. You must be outside Australia when you apply and when it is granted. Most results are immediate, but some take longer. Declare any other passports you hold. Taiwan passports qualify except official or diplomatic ones. Australian citizens cannot use an ETA.

items.name: Visitor visa (subclass 600), Tourist stream
items.who: Passport holders who cannot get an ETA or eVisitor, including Indonesia, India, China and the Philippines, must hold this visa before travel.
items.fee: Visa application charge applies. Third-party summaries of Home Affairs pricing report AUD 250 from 1 July 2026. Confirm in the official Visa Pricing Estimator before paying.
items.validity: Stay up to 12 months. The grant notice sets your stay and entry conditions.
steps: Create an ImmiAccount on the Home Affairs website.
Complete the Visitor visa (600) Tourist stream form and upload passport, funds and itinerary documents.
Pay the visa application charge and give biometrics or health checks if asked.
Travel only after you receive the grant notice. Check it in VEVO.
items.note: Apply from outside Australia. No label goes in your passport; the visa is linked to it electronically. Processing times vary, so apply early. The AUD 250 figure was not shown on the official pricing page, which loads amounts dynamically.

items.name: Incoming Passenger Card (IPC) or Australia Travel Declaration (ATD)
items.who: Almost everyone entering Australia, including Australian citizens, must complete a passenger card. The digital ATD replaces it only on eligible flights.
items.fee: Free
items.validity: One arrival
steps: If you fly Qantas into Brisbane, Sydney or Melbourne, check the Qantas app for an ATD invite up to 72 hours before departure.
If you land at Western Sydney International Airport, use the ABF ATD web form.
Otherwise fill in the paper card handed out on board, in English.
Show the paper card or ATD QR pass to officers when you exit the airport.
items.note: The ATD is still a pilot. ABF says the Qantas in-app ATD reaches Perth and Adelaide before the end of 2026, and a web form will cover all international airports and seaports before the end of 2027. The old Digital Passenger Declaration was scrapped in 2022. If your flight is cancelled, changed or diverted, you may need the paper card anyway. The ATD does not replace a visa or ETA.

AU.transit: Transit without a visa (TWOV) is allowed for citizens of many countries, including Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines, if you arrive by air, leave by air within 8 hours on a confirmed ticket and never clear immigration (for example to collect bags). Chinese and Indian ordinary passports are not on the TWOV list and need a Transit visa (subclass 771) or another Australian visa. ETA and visitor visa holders can also transit.
AU.landSea: Cruise passengers need an ETA or visa before boarding and fill in the paper Incoming Passenger Card until their port joins the digital ATD, planned before the end of 2027. Australia has no land borders.

items.name: New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority (NZeTA)
items.who: Visa waiver passport holders, including Singapore and Malaysia, must get an NZeTA before travel. Australian permanent residents and all cruise passengers also need one. Australian citizens do not.
items.fee: NZD 17 in the NZeTA app or NZD 23 on the website, plus the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy (IVL) paid at the same time.
items.validity: 2 years, multiple visits. Each visit up to 3 months (6 months for UK citizens), and no more than 6 months in any 12 months.
steps: Download the official NZeTA app or open the NZeTA website.
Choose visiting (not transit) and enter passport details exactly as printed.
Pay the NZeTA fee and the IVL together.
Allow up to 72 hours for approval. The confirmation comes by email.
items.note: The app is cheaper and can request NZeTAs for up to 10 people at once. Your passport must be valid for 3 months after you leave New Zealand. You still need the New Zealand Traveller Declaration. Kuwait visa waiver travel is suspended.

items.name: International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL)
items.who: Most visitors pay it when they request an NZeTA or apply for a visitor visa. Australian, New Zealand and many Pacific Island passport holders, and Auckland transit passengers, are exempt.
items.fee: NZD 100 per person, not refundable
items.validity: Paid once per NZeTA or visa. An NZeTA lasts 2 years.
steps: Pay the IVL in the same payment as your NZeTA or visitor visa.
Keep the receipt email. There is nothing separate to show at the border.
items.note: There is no separate IVL form. It is not refunded even if your application is declined. It rose from NZD 35 to NZD 100 on 1 October 2024. Transit NZeTAs do not include the IVL.

items.name: New Zealand Visitor Visa (online application)
items.who: Passport holders not on the visa waiver list, including Indonesia, India, China and the Philippines, must get a visitor visa before travel.
items.fee: From NZD 441 (NZD 300 fee, NZD 41 immigration levy, NZD 100 IVL)
items.validity: Stay up to 6 or 9 months as granted. You cannot work.
steps: Create an account in Immigration Online.
Fill in the Visitor Visa form and upload your passport, proof of funds and travel plans.
Pay the fee, levy and IVL online.
Wait for the decision by email. Allow about 2 weeks, longer from September to March.
items.note: Chinese citizens travelling from Australia with an eligible Australian visa can use an NZeTA instead. Cruise passengers of any nationality can use an NZeTA. INZ asks visitors to show NZD 1,000 a month, or NZD 400 a month if accommodation is prepaid.

items.name: New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD)
items.who: Everyone entering New Zealand, including New Zealand citizens, babies and children, needs one declaration each. Auckland transit passengers do not.
items.fee: Free
items.validity: One trip
steps: From 24 hours before your trip to New Zealand starts, open travellerdeclaration.govt.nz or the NZTD app.
Complete one declaration per traveller. Answers must be in English.
Submit it before you reach passport control. It links to your passport for the eGate.
items.note: A paper declaration is available on board if you cannot do it online. By sea, the window opens 24 hours before the ship leaves its last foreign port. NZeTA and visa holders must still do the NZTD.

NZ.transit: Only Auckland Airport has a transit area: stay airside, up to 24 hours, no bag collection. Visa waiver and transit visa waiver passports, including Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and China, need a transit NZeTA (NZD 17 app or NZD 23 web, no IVL). Any nationality flying to or from Australia can use a transit NZeTA with a valid Australian visa. Others, such as Indian passports not going to or from Australia, need a Transit Visa (NZD 235). Connections at other New Zealand airports count as entering the country.
NZ.landSea: Cruise and cargo ship passengers of any nationality need an NZeTA (choose visiting) before the ship departs for New Zealand, plus the IVL unless exempt. The NZTD opens 24 hours before the ship leaves its last foreign port. New Zealand has no land borders.

items.name: Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA)
items.who: Citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries, including Singapore, visiting up to 90 days without a US visa must have an approved ESTA, by air, sea or land.
items.fee: USD 40.62 from 16 October 2026 (USD 10.62 if denied). It was USD 40.27 from 1 January 2026 and USD 40 from 30 September 2025.
items.validity: 2 years or until the passport expires, whichever is first. Up to 90 days per visit.
steps: Apply on esta.cbp.dhs.gov or the official CBP ESTA Mobile app as soon as you book.
Enter passport details and answer the eligibility questions.
Pay by card and check your status. Apply no later than 72 hours before travel.
If denied, apply for a B1/B2 visa at a US embassy.
items.note: Look-alike sites charge more. Only the CBP site and app are official. A new passport needs a new ESTA. Romania is not in the program (designation rescinded May 2025). In December 2025 CBP proposed making 5 years of social media history mandatory and moving ESTA to an app only; we could not confirm it is final.

items.name: Electronic Visa Update System (EVUS) enrollment
items.who: Chinese (PRC) passport holders with a 10-year B1, B2 or B1/B2 visa must have a valid EVUS enrollment before each trip.
items.fee: USD 31.75 from 16 October 2026 (fee set by the HR-1 law)
items.validity: 2 years, or until the passport or visa expires or is replaced, whichever is first.
steps: Go to evus.gov, the only official site.
Enter passport, visa and travel details.
Pay the fee and keep the confirmation.
Enroll again after 2 years or when you get a new passport or visa.
items.note: Without a valid enrollment you cannot get a boarding pass or enter at a land port. EVUS used to be free; the fee comes from the 2025 HR-1 law and is adjusted yearly.

items.name: Provisional Form I-94 for land border entry
items.who: Non-US travellers entering by land who need an I-94, including ESTA travellers, can apply up to 7 days ahead to save time at the border.
items.fee: USD 30 (USD 6 land fee plus USD 24 HR-1 fee). No I-94 fee by air or sea.
items.validity: One entry. The I-94 records your permitted stay.
steps: Make sure your ESTA or US visa is valid first.
Apply on the CBP I-94 website or CBP mobile app up to 7 days before crossing.
Pay the fee.
Show your passport to the officer at the land port to finalise the I-94.
items.note: ESTA has been required at land borders since 1 October 2022. If you do not apply ahead, the I-94 is done at the port of entry and the same fee applies. Canadian visitors usually do not need an I-94.

US.transit: There is no airside transit in the US. Every international connection clears US immigration. Visa Waiver passports such as Singapore need an ESTA. Others need a C-1 transit visa or a B1/B2 visa, and Chinese 10-year visa holders also need EVUS.
US.landSea: ESTA is required for Visa Waiver travellers at land borders and on cruises. At land crossings an I-94 costs USD 30 and can be requested up to 7 days ahead online. No I-94 fee applies by air or sea.

items.name: Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA)
items.who: Citizens of visa-exempt countries, including Singapore, flying to or transiting through a Canadian airport need an eTA. US citizens and US green card holders are exempt.
items.fee: CAD 7
items.validity: Up to 5 years or until the passport expires, whichever is first. Stays normally up to 6 months.
steps: Apply on the official Canada.ca eTA page with the passport you will fly on.
Answer the questions and pay CAD 7.
Most approvals arrive by email within minutes. If documents are requested, instructions come within 72 hours.
Get a new eTA if you get a new passport.
items.note: Not needed by car, bus, train or boat. Romania qualifies only with an e-passport, and Taiwan only with an ordinary passport that shows the personal ID number.

items.name: eTA for select visa-required countries (instead of a visitor visa)
items.who: Citizens of 17 listed visa-required countries, including Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines, can fly to Canada on an eTA if they held a Canadian visitor visa in the last 10 years or now hold a valid US nonimmigrant visa.
items.fee: CAD 7
items.validity: Up to 5 years or until the passport expires, whichever is first.
steps: Check you held a Canadian visitor visa in the last 10 years or hold a valid US nonimmigrant visa.
Apply for the eTA on Canada.ca with the passport you will fly on.
Enter your US visa details. It must be valid on the day you apply.
If you meet neither condition, apply for a Canadian visitor visa instead.
items.note: Malaysia and Indonesia were added on 26 May 2026. Arriving by land or sea, including cruise ships, still needs a visitor visa. If your US visa is in an old passport, give that passport number in the background questions.

items.name: Advance Declaration (ArriveCAN)
items.who: Optional for travellers with a passport flying into one of 10 participating Canadian airports.
items.fee: Free
items.validity: Expires if not confirmed at a kiosk or eGate within 72 hours of submission.
steps: Open the ArriveCAN app or web version.
Submit your customs and immigration declaration up to 72 hours before your flight.
Confirm it at the airport kiosk or eGate on arrival.
items.note: Airports: Vancouver, Toronto Pearson (Terminals 1 and 3), Montreal, Winnipeg, Halifax, Quebec City, Calgary, Ottawa, Edmonton and Toronto Billy Bishop. Not usable at NEXUS kiosks. If you skip it, you declare at the kiosk. The official page is dated 2024, so the airport list may have changed.

CA.transit: Visa-exempt passports such as Singapore need an eTA even to transit. Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines can transit on an eTA if they hold a valid US visa or had a Canadian visa in the last 10 years. Indonesian, Philippine, Thai and Taiwanese passports (Transit Without Visa) and Chinese passports (China Transit Program) flying to or from the US with a valid US visa can transit visa-free for up to 24 hours, staying airside, on participating airlines at Vancouver, Toronto Pearson Terminal 1, Calgary or Winnipeg (Montreal on Air Canada for the China program). Everyone else, including Indian passports, needs a transit visa.
CA.landSea: Visa-exempt travellers need no eTA by car, bus, train or boat, except by sea from Saint Pierre and Miquelon (not cruise ships). Passports in the conditional eTA group, such as Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines, need a full visitor visa for land or sea arrivals, including cruise ships.

items.name: Forma Migratoria Múltiple Digital (FMMd)
items.who: Foreign visitors arriving by air. Nothing is filed before the flight; the officer stamps your passport, and you can then download the FMMd as proof of legal stay.
items.fee: Free to download. The federal visitor fee (DNR) is normally collected in international air tickets.
items.validity: Covers the stay granted at entry, up to 180 days. It can be downloaded once, within that period.
steps: At least 24 hours before travel, create an account on the INM services portal and register your passport.
On arrival, check the exit date the officer writes next to your passport stamp.
After entry, log in or scan the QR code at the immigration area and download your FMMd.
Keep it with your passport until you leave Mexico.
items.note: Paper FMMs are no longer issued to air arrivals. Some passports that normally need a Mexican visa are exempt if they hold a valid visa or residence from the US, Canada, UK, Japan or Schengen area; we could not open the official SRE page, so confirm with a Mexican consulate. The DNR in the ticket is per INM practice but not shown on an official 2026 page.

items.name: Forma Migratoria Múltiple electrónica (FMMe) for land entry
items.who: Foreign visitors entering Mexico by land, for example from the US or Guatemala.
items.fee: Federal visitor fee (DNR) payable online by card when it applies (stays over 7 days). Check the INM 2026 fee table for the amount.
items.validity: One entry, up to 180 days counted from the entry stamp.
steps: Fill in the FMM on the INM site with your exact passport details and port of entry.
Pay the visitor fee on the INM services portal if it applies.
Print the FMM.
Stop at the INM office at the crossing to get it stamped. Without the stamp it is not valid.
items.note: A US Passport Card works only for land crossings and the border zone, not for travel inside Mexico. Paying the fee does not guarantee entry. The 7-day fee rule comes from older INM guidance and was not confirmed on a 2026 page.

items.name: Visitax (Quintana Roo state visitor fee)
items.who: All foreign tourists who visit Quintana Roo (Cancun, Tulum, Playa del Carmen, Cozumel, Isla Mujeres, Bacalar), including children, whatever way they leave.
items.fee: About MXN 285 per person in 2026 (state government figure, no 2026 increase). The exact amount is shown on visitax.gob.mx before you pay.
items.validity: One visit to Quintana Roo
steps: Pay on visitax.gob.mx only. Look-alike sites add fees.
Enter each traveller's passport details and travel dates.
Download and keep the QR receipt for each person.
Show it if asked before airport security when you leave.
items.note: This is separate from the federal visitor fee in your air ticket. Receipts can be recovered by passport number for at least a year. The official site confirms it is mandatory but did not show the amount; the MXN 285 figure is from the Quintana Roo government press office, which we could not open directly.

MX.transit: Not confirmed on an official INM page: Mexican airports generally have no visa-free airside transit, and connecting international passengers usually clear Mexican immigration. If your passport needs a Mexican visa, have one or a valid exemption (such as a valid US visa) even for a connection.
MX.landSea: By land, get the FMMe online or at the crossing and have it stamped at the INM office. A US Passport Card is valid only in the border zone. Cruise passengers follow the cruise line's process. Visitax also applies to visitors at Cozumel and other Quintana Roo ports.

items.name: Cuba Tourist eVisa (replaces the paper tourist card)
items.who: Tourists whose passport is not visa-exempt for Cuba must hold the eVisa, mandatory since 30 June 2025. Chinese ordinary passport holders are exempt for stays up to 90 days.
items.fee: Not confirmed. The price is shown on evisacuba.cu before payment and may vary by country.
items.validity: Single entry, stay up to 90 days, extendable by 90 days.
steps: Apply on evisacuba.cu at least 72 hours before you arrive.
Pay and wait for the reply email with your 10-character visa code.
Enter that code in your D'Viajeros form.
Carry travel health insurance for your stay.
items.note: If the app's visa check says your passport is visa-free for Cuba, skip this. Sea arrivals must contact a Cuban consulate. Some sites still sell paper tourist cards or add fees; use only evisacuba.cu. We could not load evisacuba.cu directly, so the fee and stay rules come from Cuban government press items.

items.name: D'Viajeros traveller form
items.who: Every traveller entering Cuba, Cuban or foreign, including children, through airports, ports or marinas.
items.fee: Free
items.validity: One arrival
steps: Within 7 days before your trip, open dviajeros.mitrans.gob.cu.
Fill in the immigration, customs and health sections, adding your eVisa code if you need one.
Save or print the QR code.
Show the QR code at check-in and to Cuban immigration.
items.note: One form per person per arrival. It collects information for immigration, customs and the Ministry of Public Health. Avoid paid third-party sites. The 7-day window comes from a Cuban Tourism Ministry statement published by MINREX; the form site itself did not show it.

CU.transit: No official airside transit rule found. Treat a connection in Havana as an entry: complete D'Viajeros and get the eVisa if your passport is not visa-exempt. Chinese ordinary passports are exempt for transit too.
CU.landSea: The eVisa portal asks sea arrivals to contact a Cuban consulate. D'Viajeros also covers ports and marinas. Cuba has no land borders.

items.name: Check-MIG migration pre-registration
items.who: Any traveller, Colombian or foreign, entering or leaving Colombia. Migración Colombia recommends it to speed up immigration.
items.fee: Free
items.validity: The trip you register. Do it again before you leave Colombia.
steps: Between 72 hours and 1 hour before your flight, open Check-MIG from migracioncolombia.gov.co.
Enter your passport, flight and stay details.
Save or screenshot the confirmation.
Fill it in again before you leave Colombia.
items.note: Official 2025 and 2026 guidance calls it a recommendation, not a legal duty, but some airlines still ask for it at check-in, so do it anyway. Sites charging about USD 50 are not official. Frequent travellers can reuse saved data.

CO.transit: Staying in an airport's international transit zone is not entry into Colombia. Most passports can make a direct airside transit of up to 24 hours at one airport without a visa. A short list of nationalities in Resolution 5488 of 2022 needs an airport transit visa (Visa V). Changing airports means entering Colombia.
CO.landSea: Check-MIG can be filled in for any entry or exit, including land crossings. The free Biomig e-gate also works at the Rumichaca land crossing with Ecuador.

items.name: Tarjeta Andina de Migración (TAM) Virtual
items.who: Foreign visitors after entering Peru. Passports are no longer stamped on international flights, so the TAM Virtual is your official entry record.
items.fee: Free
items.validity: Shows your last entry and the days of stay granted.
steps: After passing immigration, open the TAM Virtual page.
Enter your passport details and download the record.
Check the days granted and keep a copy with your passport.
items.note: Peru has no pre-arrival form for tourists. The MigraCheck pre-registration and e-gates at Lima's new terminal are for Peruvians and resident foreigners, not tourists. Police may ask for the TAM in checks. Overstaying costs 0.1% of the UIT per day.

PE.transit: Connecting passengers at Lima stay in the international transit area and do not pass immigration; the transit charge is in the ticket. The official guide does not say whether visa-required passports are exempt for airside transit, so check with your airline if your passport needs a Peru visa.
PE.landSea: Land arrivals are recorded the same way. Download the TAM Virtual after the border post.

AR.transit: No official airside transit rule confirmed. Changing between Ezeiza (EZE) and Aeroparque (AEP) means entering Argentina, so you need whatever entry document your passport requires.
AR.landSea: No separate land or sea arrival form found. The AVE and insurance rules apply to every entry.
